_about: What Nabeel said about a game and what was done about it, shown on the Game Review page (tools/review_page.py) as a green box on that game's card. His words are kept exactly as he wrote or said them. kind: 'yours' = his own review of this game; 'also' = the same fault found here from his review of another game.

police.said: In this game you're are supposed to be chasing a criminal but the game doesn't make it clear who the criminal is. Theirs should be a clear sign that this is the car. This is the only car you should be chasing. And once the criminal gets out to run the running graphics are just awful. pilot.said:
Pilot — fixes needed

- Longer viewing distance: Render the world farther ahead so you can see distant terrain and the horizon clearly.
- Better surroundings: Improve the landscape and environment graphics. The plane itself looks fine.
- Clear starting location: Start on a recognisable runway, ready for takeoff. The current starting point looks like a mountain and is confusing.
- Takeoff and landing: Allow a complete flight from taking off to descending and successfully landing.
- Look around: Drag your thumb across the screen to move the camera naturally—right to look right, left to look left, and vertically to look up or down. Allow looking around without accidentally changing the plane’s flight controls.
- Destination waypoint: Clearly mark where you must fly and which runway you must land on, with useful direction and distance guidance.
- Mission progression: Begin with straightforward flights and landings, then make missions increasingly challenging.
- Landing feedback: Clearly recognise a successful landing and explain when an attempt fails.
pilot.did: Rebuilt. Every flight now starts lined up on runway 36 at the home airport: push the power lever up, and at ROTATE hold UP to take off. Then fly to the destination airport (its name, runway number, distance and a gold arrow are always on screen, with a gold beam over the runway and a gold ring where you line up), come down the slope (two white, two red lights) and land and stop. Drag anywhere on the open screen to look around (right looks right, up looks up); it never touches the controls, and the view swings back when you let go. You can now see 40-60 km on a clear day, with fields, woods, villages, a river, lakes and mountains on the horizon. Flight 1 is short and straight; later flights add turns, a waypoint ring, runways at an angle, crosswind and weather. A landing says BUTTER/SMOOTH/LANDED SAFELY with where you touched down; a failed one says exactly what went wrong and what to do next time.
